original_problem_scope_before: Positive scope already included long-range expanders and the repository's prior non-LRE transitive constructions (line graphs, truncations, finite/twisted fibers, same-vertex distance rewiring, and strong squares); no theorem for all bounded-degree vertex-transitive spectral expanders.
original_problem_scope_after: Adds incidence-strong products H_n=G_n boxtimes L(G_n) for fixed-degree vertex-and-edge-transitive long-range-expander bases with a uniform lower spectral edge. H_n is a bounded-degree vertex-transitive spectral expander outside every fixed long-range-expansion constant and has Salez-convention continuous-time cutoff with O(sqrt(log |V(H_n)|)) window.
explicit_d6_instance: For 6-regular edge-transitive Ramanujan Cayley bases, D=76, N=3n^2, center=(19/7)log_5 n=(19/14)log_5 N+O(1), window O(sqrt(log N)).
mechanism_progress: Proved a conditional-driver TV inequality for strong-product continuous-time walks: conditioning on the full slow-factor driver gives d_joint(t) <= d_slow^ct(a_slow t)+E[d_fast^disc(Pois(a_fast t))], while projection gives the matching lower bound. This resolves the common-clock correlation issue when one factor front dominates and the other is macroscopically post-cutoff.
obstruction_removed: The raw output-degree NBRW spectral-trace condition from the preceding NM13-01 run is not necessary and cannot follow from vertex transitivity plus spectral expansion alone. On the explicit 76-regular incidence-strong class, at r=ceil(log_75 N), the exact transitive trace C_r=sum_{i>=2}p_r(lambda_i)^2 is at least c N^kappa with kappa>0.0697, although the walk has cutoff.
trace_certificate: At least n/50 nontrivial product modes have theta>=129/304; their NBRW characteristic root satisfies z_+>79/200 and 75(79/200)^4=116850243/64000000>1, yielding kappa=1/2+2 log_75(79/200)>0.0697.
publication_novelty: UNVERIFIED; bounded repository/web search found no exact G boxtimes L(G) cutoff theorem or the polynomial NBRW-trace obstruction calculation.
residual_obstruction: A universal proof must use a factor/conditional-entropy or quotient-stable transport criterion rather than requiring small raw NBRW collision trace for the output graph. It remains open to derive such a factor-stable criterion from vertex transitivity plus ordinary spectral expansion.
next_attack: Develop an automorphism-equivariant conditional entropy/collision criterion stable under synchronous product and finite-state extensions, then test whether stabilizer-orbit (orbital) decompositions of arbitrary vertex-transitive expanders supply it.
